title: The effectiveness of exercise interventions to prevent sports injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
claims: The review analysed 25 randomised controlled trials including 26,610 participants and 3,464 injuries.
Strength training reduced sports injuries to an RR of 0.315 (95% CI 0.207-0.480); the four strength studies showed no statistical heterogeneity (I2=0%).
Proprioception training showed RR 0.550 (95% CI 0.347-0.869), and multi-exposure programmes RR 0.655 (95% CI 0.520-0.826).
Stretching showed no beneficial effect on injury risk, RR 0.963 (95% CI 0.846-1.095), based on three studies.
Preventive exercise programmes reduced acute injuries (RR 0.647, 95% CI 0.502-0.836) and overuse injuries (RR 0.527, 95% CI 0.373-0.746).
The authors concluded that all injury-prevention measures except stretching had consistently favourable estimates, and that strength training cut sports injuries to less than one-third.
